v.discovery.ui-start.text: A new pattern to discover, apprentice. Look closely at what comes next.

v.discovery.ui-try.text: Now you try. Read this word out loud.

v.discovery.ui-done.text: That is the pattern. Now you know how it works.

v.discovery.closed-review.1.text: A syllable with one vowel that ends in a consonant is closed. The consonant closes the door, so the vowel is short. Listen: cat, hop, sit.

v.discovery.closed-review.2.text: Two letters can make one sound. S and h together say sh, as in ship. C and h together say ch, as in chip.

v.discovery.closed-review.3.text: T and h say th. Put your tongue between your teeth and push the air out.

v.discovery.closed-review.4.text: At the end of a word, n and g together say ng. N and k say nk. Listen for the sound in your nose.

v.discovery.closed-review.5.text: After a short vowel, a word often ends in ck, ff, ll, ss, zz, tch or dge. They do not change the sound. Read: duck, puff, bell, catch, badge.

v.discovery.closed-review.recap.text: Remember: a closed syllable ends in a consonant, so the vowel is short. Two letters can make one sound, like sh, ch, th and ng.

v.discovery.closed-endings.1.text: An ending is added to the end of a word. After a p, k, s, sh or ch sound, the ending e d says t. Jumped, packed, wished.

v.discovery.closed-endings.2.text: After a b, g, m, n or l sound, the ending e d says d. Hugged, filled, planned, grinned.

v.discovery.closed-endings.3.text: After a t or a d, the ending e d adds a whole new part that says ed. Hunt-ed. Land-ed. Listen for two parts.

v.discovery.closed-endings.4.text: The ending s says s after a p, t or k sound, as in cats. After most other sounds it says z, as in dogs.

v.discovery.closed-endings.5.text: After s, x, sh or ch, we add e s, and it is a whole new part. Wish-es. Box-es. Bench-es. Catch-es.

v.discovery.closed-endings.recap.text: Remember: the ending e d can say t, d or ed. The ending s can say s or z. After s, x, sh or ch, es adds a part. The ending i n g keeps its own sound.

v.discovery.closed-compound.1.text: Two small words can join to make one big word. Sun and set make sunset.

v.discovery.closed-compound.2.text: Each small word is its own part. Read the first one, read the second one, then say them together.

v.discovery.closed-compound.3.text: Each small word is a closed syllable. The consonant closes the door, so each vowel is short.

v.discovery.closed-compound.recap.text: Remember: a compound word is two small words joined. Read each part, then say them together.

v.discovery.closed-vccv-double.1.text: Look at the middle of the word. Two matching consonants sit between two vowels. Split between the twins: rab-bit.

v.discovery.closed-vccv-double.2.text: Draw a line between the twin letters. Read the first part, then the second part, then blend them: mit-ten, muf-fin.

v.discovery.closed-vccv-double.3.text: The first consonant closes the door of the first part, so its vowel is short. The twin letters say just one sound.

v.discovery.closed-vccv-double.recap.text: Remember: when two matching consonants sit in the middle, split between them. The first consonant closes the door, so the vowel is short.

v.discovery.closed-vccv.1.text: Two different consonants sit between the vowels. Split between them: nap-kin.

v.discovery.closed-vccv.2.text: Cover the second part and read the first. Then cover the first and read the second. Then blend the parts together.

v.discovery.closed-vccv.3.text: Both parts end in a consonant, so the doors are closed and both vowels are short.

v.discovery.closed-vccv.recap.text: Remember: with two different consonants in the middle, split between them. Both parts are closed, so both vowels are short.

v.discovery.closed-vcccv.1.text: Sometimes three consonants sit in the middle. Keep a blend or a digraph together. Hun-dred. Os-trich.

v.discovery.closed-vcccv.2.text: If there is no blend in the middle, split after the second consonant. Sand-wich. Pump-kin.

v.discovery.closed-vcccv.3.text: Each part ends in a consonant, so each vowel is short. Read the parts, then blend.

v.discovery.closed-vcccv.recap.text: Remember: with three consonants in the middle, keep a blend together. If there is no blend, split after the second consonant.

v.discovery.closed-three.1.text: Some words have three parts. Each vowel sound is the heart of a part. Fan-tas-tic.

v.discovery.closed-three.2.text: To read a long word, divide it in two places. Split the first gap, then split the next gap.

v.discovery.closed-three.3.text: All three parts are closed, so every vowel is short. Read each part, then blend them all.

v.discovery.closed-three.recap.text: Remember: a long word may have three parts. Divide two times. All three are closed, so every vowel is short.

v.discovery.open-one.1.text: An open syllable ends in a vowel. Nothing closes the door, so the vowel says its name. Be, he, me, we.

v.discovery.open-one.2.text: The o says its name too: go, no, so.

v.discovery.open-one.3.text: The i says its name in hi. Pro and fro are open too.

v.discovery.open-one.4.text: Compare a closed word and an open word. Closed has a short vowel. Open says its name.

v.discovery.open-one.recap.text: Remember: if a syllable ends in a vowel, the door is open and the vowel says its name.

v.discovery.open-vcv.1.text: One consonant sits between two vowels. Try splitting before the consonant: ro-bot.

v.discovery.open-vcv.2.text: The first part ends in a vowel, so its door is open and the vowel says its name: ro, mu, ho.

v.discovery.open-vcv.3.text: The second part ends in a consonant, so its vowel is short: bot, sic, tel.

v.discovery.open-vcv.recap.text: Remember: one consonant between two vowels, split before it. The first part is open and says its name. The second part is closed and is short.

v.discovery.open-y.1.text: At the end of a longer word, the letter y says long e. Ba-by. Hap-py. Fun-ny.

v.discovery.open-y.2.text: At the end of a short word, the letter y says long i. My. Fly. Try. Sky.

v.discovery.open-y.3.text: In a longer word, the y makes a part of its own. Ba-by. Ti-ny. Na-vy.

v.discovery.open-y.recap.text: Remember: at the end of a short word, y says long i. At the end of a longer word, y says long e.

v.discovery.open-flex.1.text: Some words can be split two ways. Cabin can be ca-bin or cab-in. Try one way, then try the other.

v.discovery.open-flex.2.text: Try the open split first, so the vowel says its name. If it does not sound like a word you know, flip to the closed split, so the vowel is short.

v.discovery.open-flex.3.text: A part you say softly may sound like uh. Wag-on. Lem-on. Pet-al. Listen for the quiet part.

v.discovery.open-flex.recap.text: Remember: if a split does not sound like a word, flip it. Open says its name, closed is short. A quiet part may say uh.

v.discovery.vce-one.1.text: A silent e syllable has a vowel, a consonant, then an e at the end. The e is silent, and it makes the vowel say its name.

v.discovery.vce-one.2.text: The letters a, consonant, e say long a, as in cake. The letters e, consonant, e say long e, as in these.

v.discovery.vce-one.3.text: i-e says long i: bike, five, line, smile.

v.discovery.vce-one.4.text: o-e says long o: home, bone, note, stone.

v.discovery.vce-one.5.text: The letters u, consonant, e say long u, as in cube and cute. They can also say oo, as in rule and flute.

v.discovery.vce-one.recap.text: Remember: vowel, consonant, silent e. The e is silent, and the vowel says its name.

v.discovery.vce-soft.1.text: The letter c before e, i or y says s. Cell. City. Nice. We call it soft c.

v.discovery.vce-soft.2.text: The letter g before e, i or y can say j. Gem. Page. Huge. We call it soft g.

v.discovery.vce-soft.3.text: At the end of a word, c e and g e keep a silent e. It keeps the c soft and the g soft. Dance. Fence. Change.

v.discovery.vce-soft.4.text: Before a, o or u, c says k and g says g. Cat. Cup. Gap. Gum.

v.discovery.vce-soft.recap.text: Remember: c before e, i or y says s, and g before e, i or y can say j. Before a, o or u they stay hard.

v.discovery.vce-two.1.text: A silent e syllable can be the end of a long word. In-vite. Un-safe. Ex-cuse. The same rule: the vowel says its name.

v.discovery.vce-two.2.text: Divide the word first. Then look for the silent e at the end of the last part. Com-pete. Con-fuse. Ex-plode.

v.discovery.vce-two.3.text: In the letters k n, the k is silent. Knife. Knot. In w r, the w is silent. Write. Wrap.

v.discovery.vce-two.recap.text: Remember: a silent e part can finish a long word. In kn the k is silent, and in wr the w is silent.

v.discovery.vce-mix.1.text: A long word can have three parts. Divide two times. Cel-e-brate.

v.discovery.vce-mix.2.text: Look for the silent e part at the end of the word, then work backward. Nav-i-gate.

v.discovery.vce-mix.3.text: Say the middle part softly. The loud parts are the first and the last. Dom-i-nate. Ded-i-cate.

v.discovery.vce-mix.recap.text: Remember: divide a long word into parts, find the silent e part at the end, and say the middle part softly.

v.discovery.team-ai-ay.1.text: A vowel team syllable has two vowel letters working together as a team to say one sound. In rain, a and i together say long a.

v.discovery.team-ai-ay.2.text: A i goes in the middle of a word. A y goes at the end. Both say long a.

v.discovery.team-ai-ay.3.text: When you divide a long word, the team stays together. Rail-way. Ex-plain. Dis-play.

v.discovery.team-ai-ay.recap.text: Remember: a i in the middle and a y at the end are a team. They say long a.

v.discovery.team-ee-ea.1.text: Ee says long e: tree, feet, green.

v.discovery.team-ee-ea.2.text: E a often says long e too. Sea. Team. Leaf. Beach.

v.discovery.team-ee-ea.3.text: Two spellings can make the same sound. Look at the spelling to know the word. See and sea. Meet and meat. Week and weak.

v.discovery.team-ee-ea.recap.text: Remember: e e and e a are teams. They often say long e.

v.discovery.team-oa-igh.1.text: O a says long o. So does o e at the end of a word. Boat. Coat. Toe.

v.discovery.team-oa-igh.2.text: The letters i g h say long i. The g and the h are silent. Light. Right. High. Bright.

v.discovery.team-oa-igh.3.text: I e at the end of a word says long i. Pie. Tie. Lie.

v.discovery.team-oa-igh.recap.text: Remember: o a and o e say long o. I g h and i e say long i.

v.discovery.team-oo-ew.1.text: The teams o o, e w and u e can say oo, as in moon. Moon. Blew. Blue.

v.discovery.team-oo-ew.2.text: O o can also say the short sound you hear in book. Book. Look. Good. Foot.

v.discovery.team-oo-ew.3.text: Try one sound. If it does not sound like a word you know, try the other sound. Room. Cook. Boot. Took.

v.discovery.team-oo-ew.recap.text: Remember: o o has two sounds, oo as in moon and a short sound as in book. Try one, then the other.

v.discovery.team-au-oi.1.text: A u and a w both say aw. A u sits inside a word, and a w ends a word. Sauce. Haul. Saw. Draw.

v.discovery.team-au-oi.2.text: O i and o y both say oy. O i sits inside a word, and o y ends a word. Coin. Oil. Boy. Toy.

v.discovery.team-au-oi.3.text: A w and o y often end a part in a long word. Aw-ful. En-joy. An-noy.

v.discovery.team-au-oi.recap.text: Remember: a u and a w say aw. O i and o y say oy. The letters inside a word are u and i. The letters at the end are w and y.

v.discovery.team-ou-ow.1.text: O u says ow, as in out. Cloud. House. Mouth. Found.

v.discovery.team-ou-ow.2.text: O w can say ow too. Cow. Down. Town. Brown. Owl.

v.discovery.team-ou-ow.3.text: O w can also say long o. Snow. Grow. Slow. Yellow.

v.discovery.team-ou-ow.4.text: Ow has two sounds. Try ow first. If it does not sound like a word you know, flip to long o. Cow and crow. Brown and blown.

v.discovery.team-ou-ow.recap.text: Remember: o u says ow. O w has two sounds, ow and long o. Try one, and flip if it is not a word.

v.discovery.team-mix.1.text: E a can also say short short e. Head. Bread. Breath. Thread.

v.discovery.team-mix.2.text: P h says f. Phone. Photo. Graph. Dolphin.

v.discovery.team-mix.3.text: Sometimes two vowels side by side are not a team. They belong to different parts. Li-on. Gi-ant. Du-et.

v.discovery.team-mix.4.text: Try the team sound first. If it does not sound like a word you know, try the other sound, or split between the two vowels.

v.discovery.team-mix.recap.text: Remember: e a can say long e or short e. P h says f. Two vowels may split into two parts.

v.discovery.r-ar-or.1.text: An r syllable has a vowel followed by r. The r changes the vowel sound, so it is not short and it is not long.

v.discovery.r-ar-or.2.text: Ar says ar, as in car. Open your mouth wide.

v.discovery.r-ar-or.3.text: Or says or, as in fork. Round your lips.

v.discovery.r-ar-or.4.text: In long words, the vowel and the r stay together when you divide. Gar-den. Tar-get. For-est.

v.discovery.r-ar-or.recap.text: Remember: a vowel followed by r makes a new sound. A r says ar and o r says or.

v.discovery.r-er-ir-ur.1.text: E r, i r and u r all say the same sound. Fern. Bird. Turn.

v.discovery.r-er-ir-ur.2.text: There are three spellings for one sound. You cannot hear which one it is, so look at the letters. First. Shirt. Third. Hurt. Surf. Burst.

v.discovery.r-er-ir-ur.3.text: E r is the most common spelling at the end of a word. After. Sister. Winter. Number.

v.discovery.r-er-ir-ur.recap.text: Remember: e r, i r and u r all say the same sound. A word ending in the sound usually uses the letters e r.

v.discovery.r-mix.1.text: Long words can have an r part and other parts. Divide first, then name each part. Car-pen-ter.

v.discovery.r-mix.2.text: Keep each vowel and r together. Do not split them. Gar-den-ing. Mar-ket-ing. Re-port-ing.

v.discovery.r-mix.3.text: The last part is often quiet. Car-pen-ter. Yes-ter-day. Say it softly.

v.discovery.r-mix.recap.text: Remember: divide a long word, keep each vowel and r together, and say the last part softly.

v.discovery.le-one.1.text: A consonant plus l e at the end of a word is a part of its own. Ta-ble.

v.discovery.le-one.2.text: Count back three letters from the end of the word. That last part is the consonant plus l e. Can-dle. Pur-ple.

v.discovery.le-one.3.text: If the part before ends in a vowel, it says its name: ta-ble. If it ends in a consonant, the vowel is short: can-dle.

v.discovery.le-one.recap.text: Remember: count back three letters from the end. Consonant plus l e is the last part.

v.discovery.le-double.1.text: A double consonant before l e. Split between the twins. Lit-tle. Bub-ble. Pud-dle.

v.discovery.le-double.2.text: The twin letters close the door of the first part, so its vowel is short. Bub. Pud. Lit.

v.discovery.le-double.3.text: Compare maple and apple. With one consonant, the vowel says its name. With twin consonants, the vowel is short.

v.discovery.le-double.4.text: The letters c k count as a double. Buckle. Tickle. Pickle. The vowel is short.

v.discovery.le-double.recap.text: Remember: twin consonants before l e close the first part, so the vowel is short. C k counts as a double.

v.discovery.le-mix.1.text: Now you know six kinds of syllables. Each one tells you how to read the vowel.

v.discovery.le-mix.2.text: Spec-ta-cle has three parts. The first is closed, the second is open, and the last is a consonant plus l e.

v.discovery.le-mix.3.text: Read a long word like a bridge. Divide it, name each part, read each part, then blend. If it does not sound like a word, flip a vowel sound and try again.

v.discovery.le-mix.recap.text: Remember: divide, name each part, read each part, then blend. If it is not a word, flip a vowel sound and try again.
